review_findings: Two direct report impacts (funds_stranded, liquidity_reduced) are acknowledged but left unformalized with no claim representing them.
The single formalized claim (core_claim) covers only the accounting/balance divergence, not the report's stated permanent locking or liquidity reduction.
The report's direct impact (silent token loss and unaccounted tokens) is acknowledged but not formalized; core_claim only formalizes the intermediate one-token-processed outcome.
Splitting the single shadow impact into two unformalized items plus one formalized intermediate outcome creates confusing coverage; the formalized item is not the report's stated harm.
lifecycle_broken and liquidity_locked impacts are acknowledged but not represented by any claim (unformalized).
min_check_pass_lot_fail is listed as an impact coverage item but is a mechanism/context, not a distinct direct impact; it is unformalized and not represented by a claim.

Two distinct shadow impacts (stuck orders vs permanently broken lifecycle) are merged into one lifecycle_broken row, and two liquidity impacts merged into one liquidity_locked row, reducing granularity.
The conditional impact that bribes would be sent to address(0) and burned if access control were bypassed is omitted from coverage entirely.
bribes_lost and owner_zero_after_burn are acknowledged but left unformalized, so only one of four direct impacts is formalized.
Two of the three direct report impacts (aa_features_bricked and default_state_incompatible) are acknowledged but left unformalized with no claim_ids; only recovered_not_owner is formalized.
The formal plan's limitations explicitly state aa_features_bricked and default_state_incompatible are deferred and not implied by the claim, confirming partial coverage.
